claims.text: The framework employs a Question-Answer Generation, Sorting, and Evaluation (Q-S-E) methodology to enable quantitative hallucination detection in text summaries.
The framework incorporates an iterative hallucination resolution mechanism leveraging LLMs to modify summaries.

evidence.description: This paper introduces a hallucination detection and mitigation framework that employs a Question-Answer Generation, Sorting, and Evaluation (Q-S-E) methodology to enable the quantitative detection of hallucinations in summaries.

Leveraging LLMs, the framework incorporates an iterative hallucination resolution mechanism, which enhances the transparency of the modification process and improves the faithfulness of text summarization.

methodologies.name: Q-S-E Hallucination Detection and Mitigation Framework
methodologies.description: A framework combining Question-Answer Generation, Sorting, and Evaluation (Q-S-E) with an iterative LLM-based hallucination resolution mechanism.

limitations.text: Existing methods exhibit limitations in effectively detecting and mitigating hallucinations, often lacking transparency in their underlying mechanisms.
